what_it_does: This paper describes a tiny isolated power converter—a device that steps voltage down from a source to a chip—built directly on chip with only 2 watts of power loss. The problem: when you convert power, the switching control signal (PWM, a rapid on-off pattern) leaks electromagnetic noise into the environment (EMI) and back into the power supply, requiring bulky external filters that waste energy. This design buries a transformer inside the chip itself to cancel out the noise-causing currents before they escape, achieving compliance with strict EMI standards while keeping the output voltage rock-steady (ripple under 5 millivolts).
